raw_response:
I farm only 2.0 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it. I have 40 years of experience and access to well irrigation, so I will stay with a stable, practical approach instead of taking risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen for strong tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus to support roots, and some potassium to keep the crop sturdy. I will irrigate a few key times because water is available from my well and that is important for wheat here. I will do moderate pesticide use, only enough to control the usual diseases, weeds, and insects. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 2.0 mu because hybrid maize gives me better yield and fits my rotation. For maize, I will keep fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate during the main water-demand periods. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient and suitable for my small farm. My goal is steady yield, controlled cost, and reliable production from both crops.
